Logistic regression models a binary outcome, such as whether a patient recovers, from one or more predictors.
Its fitted coefficients are maximum likelihood estimates,
so the likelihood theory of [Introduction to maximum likelihood](intro-MLEs.qmd#sec-intro-MLEs) gives them standard errors, confidence intervals and tests.
This page specializes that theory to the logistic model and introduces the deviance,
the measure of fit that the likelihood ratio test of a logistic model is built from [@wikipedia_likelihood_ratio_test].
